bullets: How information in DNA becomes a protein, and how alleles are shuffled and passed on: monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, sex-linked inheritance, and what mutations really do
slides.heading: JC H2 biology -- genetics: from DNA to inheritance
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one thread from DNA to inheritance - transcription and translation, two kinds of cross, a sex-linked case, and a mutation trap to correct at the end.

bullets: Describe the central dogma: DNA is transcribed into mRNA and translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome
Predict offspring genotypes and phenotypes for monohybrid crosses (3:1) and dihybrid crosses (9:3:3:1), including sex-linked inheritance
Judge claims about mutations using evidence: most are neutral, some are harmful, and a few are beneficial
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things, including judging the mutation trap.

bullets: Both parents carry one faulty allele but show no symptoms themselves
Will every child be affected, none of them, or is it a matter of chance - and can you put a number on it?
slides.heading: Two healthy carrier parents: what are the odds for their child?
slides.notes: Ask the class to commit to a guess before any definitions: every child, no child, or one in four? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the Punnett square in scene s2 settles this exactly.

bullets: Every cross in this lesson is the same move: each parent passes on one allele per gene, chosen at random, and the Punnett square lists every equally likely combination
Inheritance ratios are probabilities, not promises: 3:1 and 9:3:3:1 describe what large numbers of offspring approach
slides.heading: One idea, five scenes: alleles combine by chance
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea: do not memorise ratios as magic numbers - build the square, count the boxes, and the ratio falls out.

bullets: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus: the mRNA carries one gene's instructions out through a nuclear pore
At a ribosome the mRNA is translated: its codons are read in order and amino acids are joined into a polypeptide chain
slides.heading: Central dogma: DNA makes protein
slides.notes: Narrate the information flow: DNA to mRNA to protein, one way only. Say: transcription copies, translation builds - keep those two words separate.

bullets: Cross two heterozygotes, Aa x Aa: each parent passes on A or a with equal chance, giving AA, Aa, Aa and aa in the four boxes
Three boxes in four show the dominant trait - a 3:1 phenotype ratio - while the genotypes underneath run 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa
slides.heading: Monohybrid cross: the 3:1 ratio
slides.notes: Build the square box by box and count out loud. Say: the 3:1 you see hides a 1:2:1 you must be able to state.

bullets: Track two genes on different chromosomes at once, such as seed shape and seed colour: the genes assort independently, so each parent makes four gamete types
Sixteen equally likely boxes fall into four phenotype classes in the ratio 9:3:3:1 - both dominants, two mixed classes, and the double recessive
slides.heading: Dihybrid cross: 9:3:3:1
slides.notes: Stress the condition: independent assortment holds because the genes are on different chromosomes. Count the classes with the class: 9, then 3, then 3, then 1.

bullets: Haemophilia is carried on the X chromosome: a carrier mother (X^H X^h) crossed with a normal father (X^H Y) passes the faulty allele to half her sons on average
Sons show the trait when they inherit the faulty X because the Y carries no allele to mask it, while daughters who inherit it are usually carriers
slides.heading: Sex-linked inheritance
slides.notes: Follow the X chromosomes, not just the letters. Say: a son gets his only X from his mother, so her carrier status decides his risk.

bullets: The trap claim in full: Every mutation harms the organism. It feels true because the word mutation suggests breakage - but the evidence in this scene says otherwise
Most mutations are neutral: only some are harmful, and a rare few are the raw material of evolution
slides.heading: A common mistake: mutations are always harmful
slides.notes: Name the trap out loud: Every mutation harms the organism. Then land the correction with the scene: a changed protein can still do the same job, so most changes alter nothing that matters.

bullets: Gametes are A and a from each parent; the four boxes give AA, Aa, Aa, aa, so the chance of an affected (aa) child is 1 in 4 and of a carrier (Aa) child is 1 in 2
Phenotypes run 3 unaffected : 1 affected, matching the 3:1 ratio from scene s2 - the same square answers genotype and phenotype questions
slides.heading: Worked example: the carrier cross, Aa x Aa
slides.notes: Talk through the square slowly and answer both questions from it: first count genotypes, then group them into phenotypes. Say: never quote 3:1 for a genotype question.

bullets: A carrier mother (X^H X^h) and a normal father (X^H Y) have a son. What is the chance he has haemophilia? Show the cross.
Careful - a classmate says: Every mutation harms the organism. Correct them in one sentence, naming what most mutations actually do
slides.heading: Your turn: build the square, then judge the claim
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them on the son's 1 in 2 chance first, then on the exact sentence they used to correct the claim: Every mutation harms the organism.

bullets: On your own: state the genotype and phenotype ratios for Aa x Aa, and the phenotype ratio for a dihybrid cross with independent assortment
Watch out for the trap one last time: Every mutation harms the organism. Say what most mutations do, and what a rare few provide
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for 1:2:1 and 3:1 in your first answer and 9:3:3:1 alongside it, plus one clear neutral-mutation sentence in your second. Anyone repeating the claim Every mutation harms the organism. needs the trap scene again.
